the business cycle is a key determinant of income inequality.
the inequality of income and consumption rises in the United States during the upturn of the business cycle, and the inequality of consumption falls during the downturn of the business cycle.
the relationship between the business cycle and inequality is not a simple one.

the following issues: (a) the relationship between inequality and growth, (b) the relationship between the business cycle and inequality, and (c) the relationship between financial crises and inequality.
the role of income inequality and its impact on macroeconomic stability.
understanding the role of inequality in the business cycle and how inequality affects economic growth.

the relationship between income inequality and the business cycle is that income inequality increases during economic expansions and decreases during economic recessions.
the business cycle is a recurring period of alternating economic expansion and contraction that results from the interaction of supply and demand.
the business cycle is a fluctuation of the economic activity in an economy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inequality of the distribution of income and wealth in society has been rising in the United States for decades, and the gap between the richest Americans and the rest of the country has been growing.
the current business cycle is a result of a lack of consumer spending.
inequality and economic growth are closely related, but the nature of the relation is complex and not well understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inequality is a two-edged sword: rising inequality can be both a cause and consequence of economic expansion.
rising inequality is not only bad for the poor, but also bad for the economy as a whole.
the economy’s business cycle is not just a matter of aggregate demand and supply shocks, but also of distributional shocks, which are often cyclical in nature.
